::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at Part 2](../../slides/housing-one-day.html#/part-2-the-claim-and-its-estimand){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

The first case of the term begins in earnest. In class you write the estimand statement behind the claim, finish the causal graph of the experiment, and reproduce the value that Multi100 recorded for one of the five analysts, everyone at the same moment. The modules of the week are the methods that the claim is argued with: what random assignment buys in an audit experiment, the models for a yes-or-no outcome, and the causal graph that shows why a comparison among the replies alone is no longer protected by the random assignment. Read the exercise overview before the class meets, and the modules after it.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Exercise overview](../../cases/housing/exercise.qmd) | Before class. The claim, the table of what the five Multi100 analysts found, and the five tasks that the next two weeks work through. | 15 minutes |
| Slides, Part 2 | In class. The paper of the original authors (OAs), its design and the claim as SCORE selected it, with its two ellipses; the five analysts placed by their gaps; the estimands run, with the red-card study as the example; the causal-graph crash course; and the estimand statement that the class writes, holds and sends together. | 45 minutes |
| Task 2 in your report or working script, or [Browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-2-data) Task 2 | In class. Count the emails that bounced, the replies, the replies with a greeting code and the greetings by name for each name. Write the [estimand statement](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-2-estimand-and-graph) with every bracket filled, saying which emails you count. Open `R/dag_starter.R`, keep the arrows that you are willing to defend, and run `adjustmentSets(dag)` and `paths(dag, Z = "reply")`. | 25 minutes |
| Slides, the opening of [Part 3](../../slides/housing-one-day.html#/part-3-reproduction-and-exploration), and Task 3 in your report or [Browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction) | In class. The instruction of Task 2 of Multi100 read word for word, then the reproduction: read the public file `audit_original.csv`, keep the replies with a greeting code, build the two-by-two table and pass it to `chisq.test()`. It gives $\chi^2$ = 14.265 on 558 replies, the value that Multi100 recorded for analyst 8PTRZ. Then the slide on why it is not 14.95, and why everyone in the class got the same value while the five analysts did not. | 35 minutes |
| [Audit experiments](../../companion/experiments.qmd), sections 1 to 4 | Audit and correspondence studies of discrimination; what random assignment buys, with a check of balance; names as treatments; and why a comparison among replies needs care, with a bound on how far a change in who replied could go. | 60 minutes |
| [Binary outcomes](../../companion/binary-outcomes.qmd), sections 1 to 7 | A 0/1 outcome and its share; the difference in proportions and its standard error; the linear probability model with HC2 standard errors; logistic regression; odds ratios against percentage points and average marginal effects; why a covariate changes an odds ratio even in an experiment; and the methods side by side. | 75 minutes |
| [Causal graphs and adjustment sets](../../companion/dags.qmd), sections 1 to 5 | What an arrow commits you to; confounders, mediators and colliders; why comparing greetings among replies conditions on a consequence of the name; the graph of the case; and what counting every delivered email changes. | 50 minutes |
| [Decision map](../../cases/housing/map.qmd) | Every decision between the data and a result, in the order in which an analyst meets it, with what each option does to the estimand statement and to the estimate. It prepares Task 4 of next week. | 20 minutes |

**By the end of the session** you have the estimand behind the claim written in one sentence, a graph that holds only the arrows you are willing to defend, two sentences on what a comparison among the replies conditions on, and $\chi^2$ = 14.265 reproduced yourself, with the reason why it is not 14.95.
